hook.text: Water expands when it warms—this simple physics caused about half of sea level rise in the 20th century.

buildup.text: No extra water is added—the same water just takes up more space as its temperature rises.

discovery.text: Thermal expansion has raised global sea level about 8 cm since 1970—and the rate is increasing.

twist.text: Deep-ocean warming means expansion will continue for centuries—even if surface warming stopped today.

climax.text: Combined with ice melt, total sea level rise could reach 1 meter by 2100—threatening coastal cities.

punchline.text: Warming water swells the sea—no melting required.

quiz.question: What is thermal expansion?
options: Water expanding in volume as it warms
